title: DiaLong: Benchmarking Reminiscence in Long-Context Dialogues
abstract: arXiv:2610.25463v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: How well can transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs) retain and recall memories in long contexts of dialogue? LLMs are known to forget long-range factual information in their context, yet the field lacks a comprehensive benchmark to quantitatively assess these shortcomings. We present DiaLong, a long-context dialogue dataset and accompanying memory task that standardizes evaluation in this space. It consists of 100 unique conversations created by humans and then augmented with LLMs, extending beyond lengths found in existing datasets. Our selected memory task is fact recall: classify 40 candidate facts about a dialogue as true or false. This task directly probes the model's ability to actively retain and retrieve information, serving as a critical measure of memory within extended conversational contexts. In testing both the latest LLMs and proposed memory enhancements on DiaLong, we demonstrate that more work needs to be done

translated_title: DiaLong：长上下文对话中记忆回溯能力的基准测试
translated_abstract: 基于Transformer的大语言模型（LLM）在长对话上下文中保持和回忆记忆的能力究竟如何？众所周知，LLM会遗忘其上下文中的长距离事实信息，然而该领域一直缺乏一个能够定量评估这些缺陷的综合性基准。我们提出了DiaLong，这是一个长上下文对话数据集及配套的记忆任务，用于将该领域的评估标准化。该数据集由100个由人类创建、随后借助LLM进行增强的独特对话组成，其长度超越了现有数据集中的对话长度。我们选择的记忆任务是事实回忆：将关于某段对话的40个候选事实判断为真或假。该任务直接探测模型主动保持和检索信息的能力，是衡量扩展对话上下文中记忆能力的关键指标。通过在DiaLong上测试最新的LLM以及已提出的记忆增强方法，我们证明了该领域仍有大量工作需要完成。
tldr: 提出DiaLong基准，包含100个超长人类对话及事实回忆判别任务，用以定量评估大语言模型在长上下文对话中主动保持和检索信息的能力，测试表明现有模型及记忆增强方法仍远未达标。
en_tdlr: We introduce DiaLong, a benchmark of 100 extended human-created dialogues with a fact-recall task to quantitatively assess LLMs' ability to actively retain and retrieve information in long-context conversations, showing that current models and memory enhancements still fall short.
